text:
maria: Quick sync — AcmeCorp POC kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. Main asks: streaming SDK ramp, tool/function-calling examples, structured JSON output schema, and pricing/latency expectations.

alex: Thanks — I'll own SDK snippets and a minimal streaming example. Any constraints on languages?

maria: They prefer Go + Node first. They'll try Rust later.

devon: For streaming: recommend SSE path first (simpler), websocket if they need bi-directional. Watch for backpressure at >200 qps per connection.

sophie: For function/tool calling: send them a sample where we return a single top-level `tool_results` array (keeps validation simple). Also include a fallback plain-text message when JSON parse fails.

alex: Drafting snippets now. Quick Node stream snippet:

```js
const stream = client.responses.stream({model: 'rwd-stream-1', input: '...'});
for await (const part of stream) { process.stdout.write(part.delta); }
```

alex: I'll also add a Go SSE example and the minimal retry/backoff config.

maria: Security Q: they require KMS integration + SOC2 attestation. Can we provide a quick summary for their security questionnaire?

devon: Yes — we have SOC2 + optional customer-managed KMS via Redwood Private. For hosted: data is encrypted at rest; we can provide KMS rotation docs and access control matrix. I'll drop the questionnaire snippets in the ticket.

sophie: Also call out ephemeral creds for connectors. For on-prem they want a short-lived token workflow. We have an example using short-lived JWT from our auth service — link and sample curl will help.

presales-bot: Created POC ticket POC-4321 and attached template: https://redwood.internal/poc/POC-4321

maria: Pricing note — they asked for an estimate for 200k tokens/month with streaming. Bound to a committed Reserved plan vs hosted usage?

alex: Rough calc: streaming reduces token overhead slightly but pricing depends on model and quantization. I'll send a baseline: hosted per-token estimate + sample Reserved bucket cost for 3-month pilot.

devon: Operational blocker flagged: AcmeCorp uses IP-allowlist + corporate proxy. Need handshake docs for proxy + example of preflight handshake using `x-redwood-bridge` header.

sophie: Also add guidance on structured output validation: include a small JSON Schema and an example fuzz prompt set to detect regressions. We'll suggest an eval job run nightly.

maria: Can you include canary rollback guidance? They want to test tool-calls with production traffic subset.

devon: Recommend a canary route: 5% traffic to new model variant, automatic fallback to `rwd-compat-lite` on timeout >250ms or 5xx errors. Document the route policy in the runbook.

alex: Putting together a one-page integration runbook: 1) quickstart Node + Go snippets, 2) SSE vs WS decision table, 3) toolcall schema + fallback, 4) security checklist, 5) pricing ranges, 6) canary steps.

maria: Perfect. Can we have the runbook and snippets posted before the 10am kickoff?

alex: Yes — I'll post the PR in ~30m.

sophie: I'll attach JSON Schema and the sample eval prompts.

devon: I'll drop the proxy handshake example + KMS info.

presales-bot: POC-4321 updated: alex (sdk), devon (infra), sophie (evals/security) assigned.

maria: Awesome. Last ask: can we include a short snippet showing function-call response with structured output and a graceful non-JSON fallback?

alex: Will include both. Example preview in the runbook: {"tool_results":[{"id":"extract","payload":{"entities":[...]}}]} + fallback to `raw_text` field.

maria: Thank you team — see you at 10. :thumbsup:
